item.title: Sphera Media Lab 2026: Open Call for Masterclasses and Keynotes
item.description:
Organisation: European Lab (Arty Farty) and the Sphera Network, coordinated by Medianes

Location: LaVallee, Rue Adolphe Lavallee 39, 1080 Brussels, Belgium. Proposals are accepted regardless of where you are based, but they should reflect a European perspective.

Award: Selected contributors receive a fee plus travel to Brussels and accommodation, all covered by the organisers. The fee amount is not published in the call. No submission fee.

Duration: One-day event on 3 December 2026; contributors deliver a single masterclass or keynote

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

European Lab and the Sphera Network are opening submissions for the discourse programme of the next Sphera Media Lab, the annual forum for people defending independent media in Europe. THEMES: technological independence (sovereignty, tools, mutualisation); economic independence (cooperative models); editorial independence (press freedom, resisting the far right). FORMATS SOUGHT: masterclasses, led by an expert sharing advanced knowledge, technique and hands-on insight; and keynotes, inspiring talks grounded in a specific case study. WHO CAN PROPOSE: media outlets, associations, researchers and professionals. The organisers state they pay particular attention to parity and diversity across their programmes and ask that proposals take those criteria into account. WHAT IS COVERED: selected contributors travel to Brussels with transport, accommodation and a fee covered. THE EVENT: Sphera Media Lab 2026 runs on 3 December 2026 at LaVallee in Brussels, a full day of conferences, masterclasses and workshops for independent media professionals from across Europe, alongside the premiere of a documentary on threats facing European journalists. APPLICATION: submit your masterclass or keynote proposal via the Typeform at arty-farty.typeform.com/to/xnDikGGM before 31 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Extra Teeth: Open Submissions for Fiction and Nonfiction (paid)
item.description:
Organisation: Extra Teeth

Location: Scottish magazine with an international outlook. Open to writers anywhere; Scottish writers especially championed, and submissions from underrepresented groups especially welcome.

Award: GBP 200 per piece selected for the magazine, plus two copies of the issue. Four pieces are also selected for the With Bite Substack at GBP 150 each. Guest illustrator (one per issue) is paid GBP 943.90. Paid by bank transfer within 30 days of a signed publishing agreement. No submission fee.

Duration: Per-issue publication; submissions accepted during open submission periods.

Deadline: 14 Dec 2026

Extra Teeth is a Scottish literary magazine with an international outlook, paying for fiction and nonfiction. Submissions are currently open. No theme is set per issue; send your best work on any topic. Pieces should be 800 to 4,000 words, previously unpublished, submitted as a Word document (standard font, size 12, double line spacing) titled with 'F' for fiction or 'NF' for nonfiction followed by your name, plus a title sheet (name, address, word count, bio under 100 words); cover letters are not required. Send one piece only per submission period to submissions@extrateeth.co.uk with 'SHORT STORY: TITLE' or 'ESSAY: TITLE' in the subject line; secondary submissions are deleted. Copyright remains with the author. Work in translation is accepted with the necessary permissions. The magazine does not currently publish poetry, scripts or artwork (aside from its guest illustrator). PAYMENT: GBP 200 per piece for the magazine plus two contributor copies; four pieces are also chosen for the With Bite Substack at GBP 150 each. AI POLICY: no AI-written work is published or considered. ILLUSTRATORS: one guest illustrator is commissioned per issue (paid GBP 943.90); send work to hello@extrateeth.co.uk with 'ILLUSTRATOR' in the subject line; marginalised illustrators especially encouraged. Allow eight weeks after the submission period before querying. Check the submissions page for current open periods.

Open call details

item.title: Hellmouth Magazine: Volume 3 "Metamorphosis" - Call for Submissions
item.description:
Organisation: Hellmouth Magazine

Location: Knoxville, TN, USA; Southeast US focus for reviews, but national and international exceptions considered. Remote submissions.

Award: $50 honorarium upon publication. No submission fee.

Duration: One-time publication in Volume 3.

Deadline: Closed 20 Jun 2026

Hellmouth Magazine, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit arts and culture publication based in Knoxville, TN, is seeking submissions for Volume 3 on the theme of "Metamorphosis." The magazine publishes twice annually, covering experimental essays, critical art writing, reviews, interviews, and visual art. HONORARIUM: $50 upon publication. CATEGORIES OPEN: Reviews (exhibitions, gallery events, artist shows, cultural happenings -- Southeast focus but national/international exceptions welcomed; 500-750 words); Interviews (artists living or dead; video interviews also welcome; open word count); Art Writing (academic or experimental essays on contemporary or historical art -- artists, movements, zeitgeist, concepts, theories; 1,200+ words); Visual Art (digital output or print; best submitted alongside an upcoming show or event). FICTION & POETRY: closed for this volume. THEME: Metamorphosis as transformative vehicle -- post-Anthropocentric systems, chimeras, the post-human and transhuman, cultural and political shapeshifting, transformation through art and literature in the wake of collective trauma. All pitches should be approximately 500 words. Read recent issues before submitting. Submissions due 20 June 2026. Submit at https://www.hellmouthmag.com/submit.

Open call details

item.title: CRAFT Literary: Creative Nonfiction (Year-Round Submissions)
item.description:
Organisation: CRAFT Literary

Location: Online (US-based, international writers accepted)

Award: $200 per original creative-nonfiction piece ($100 for flash). No submission fee.

Duration: Rolling / year-round

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Online literary magazine paying for original creative nonfiction (essays and flash), open year-round with no submission fee. Useful, low-barrier way for an emerging writer to publish a standalone critical/creative-nonfiction piece and build a publication record toward a book. ELIGIBILITY: open to any emerging or established author; submissions accepted from international writers. Creative categories are open on a rolling basis year-round.

item.title: C Magazine: Call for Pitches (Art Writing & Criticism)
item.description:
Organisation: C Magazine

Location: Toronto, Canada (open to writers internationally)

Award: 35-45 cents/word; print reviews flat CAD $430; online reviews CAD $210. No fee.

Duration: Rolling (themed print deadlines plus continuous online pitches)

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Contemporary art magazine commissioning paid art writing and criticism, with pitches accepted on an ongoing basis (online reviews/pitches continuous; themed print issues have set deadlines, e.g. the Spring issue around 15 September 2026). A direct paid outlet for criticism on digital, new-media and AI art. ELIGIBILITY: writers at all experience levels are invited; not restricted to Canada. Mostly pitch-based, with short online reviews accepted unsolicited.

item.title: The Stinging Fly: Open Submissions (Creative Nonfiction)
item.description:
Organisation: The Stinging Fly

Location: Dublin, Ireland (international submissions)

Award: Paid on acceptance: nonfiction approx. EUR 50/page (minimum EUR 375, maximum EUR 1,250). No submission fee.

Duration: Per piece; submissions accepted in timed windows

Deadline: 23 Nov 2026

Leading Irish literary magazine that publishes and pays for creative nonfiction (as well as fiction and poetry), with a stated particular interest in promoting new and emerging writers. A clean, no-fee, internationally-open outlet for a standalone critical/creative-nonfiction piece. ELIGIBILITY: Irish and international writers; debut-friendly, no published-book requirement. Submissions are accepted in specific windows; the next nonfiction window runs Monday 9 November to Monday 23 November 2026 (closes 5pm Irish time) for the Summer 2027 issue.

item.title: Tractor Beam: Issue 6 'The Water Issue' - Call for Submissions
item.description:
Organisation: Tractor Beam

Location: Online publication (remote submissions; geographic eligibility not stated)

Award: $1,000 USD per accepted submission. Accepted work is considered for publication online (Tractor Beam website and Substack) and, in some cases, for one-off printed editions. Stories may also be considered for the Protopian Prize with contributor consent. No submission fee mentioned.

Duration: One-off published piece (no residency component)

Deadline: Closed 30 Jun 2026

Tractor Beam's sixth issue, themed around water in soil, growth, land and ecosystems large and small, is open for submissions. Editors are seeking anti-apocalyptic visions that explore the future of water in farming and food production, island ecologies, hybrid sea-soil technologies, the people who move water and the people water moves, plus stories about drought, diaspora and what gets carried downstream. FORMAT: stories under 6,000 words; comics 12-16 panels. Submissions accepted via the call page on Tractor Beam's Substack.

Open call details
